statusDetail: Coverage complete for 58 checks across four representative public templates plus an invalid-route recovery state. Authenticated taxpayer-only screens were excluded because credentials were not supplied.

page.notes: The entry origin redirects through HTTP back to HTTPS /services/login. Public routes are client-rendered AngularJS templates.

paths.description: Entry URL redirects to the public login template, representing authentication and account recovery. Authenticated taxpayer-only routes were not covered because no credentials were supplied.
Public Track Application Status form, representing a short status lookup journey.
Public Search HSN Code form, representing search and content-heavy results guidance.
Public grievance form, representing the longest high-risk data-entry flow.
Deliberately invalid route, representing HTTP/navigation failure recovery.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus can disappear and hidden controls remain tabbable
findings.evidence: The focus probe found the visible Services anchor with outline none and many zero-size menu links in the focus sequence; the toggle button was also zero-size at desktop.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :focus-visible with a persistent high-contrast indicator and remove hidden menu descendants from the tab order.

findings.summary: Load performance misses the Core Web Vitals bar
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 8.5 s, TBT 770 ms and CLS 0.146; the first-party trace corroborated LCP 2.50 s and TBT 305 ms on the local run.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP chain, remove redirect latency, defer non-critical scripts and reserve layout space.

findings.summary: Templates shift substantially during load
findings.evidence: Layout observers measured CLS 0.151 on login, 0.143 on status, 0.303 on grievance and 0.990 on HSN search; Lighthouse identified form/footer shifts and unsized icons.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions for header, form and footer regions and add explicit image dimensions and stable font fallbacks.

findings.summary: Legacy script work blocks the main thread
findings.evidence: Trace recorded a 355 ms long task and 305 ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 2.6 s main-thread work with 1.79 s script evaluation.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the monolithic framework bundle, defer route-specific code and break expensive initialization into scheduled tasks.

findings.summary: Most of large shared bundles are unused on login
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 235 KiB unused JavaScript, including 77% of a 220 KiB bundle, plus 22 KiB unused CSS and 22 KiB minification savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship route-level bundles, remove legacy/duplicate framework code and purge unused CSS.

findings.summary: Landmark and heading structure is incomplete
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found no main landmark and a heading-order failure (Login begins at h4); the focus probe also found hidden and outline-less controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a main landmark, use a sequential heading hierarchy and repair visibility-aware focus management.

findings.summary: Password managers are deliberately obstructed
findings.evidence: The password input has autocomplete="off" and data-ng-paste="$event.preventDefault()"; Lighthouse flags paste prevention, and three large scripts reference missing source maps.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow paste, use autocomplete="current-password", support password managers and publish valid source maps.

findings.summary: An insecure redirect and cookie weaken an HTTPS login
findings.evidence: Lighthouse observed an HTTP redirect hop; the cookie audit found Lang without Secure and both cookies set SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Redirect directly over HTTPS and set Secure with the least-permissive appropriate SameSite value on all cookies.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and blocks secure assistance
findings.evidence: The login surface exposes only username/password, disables autocomplete and blocks password paste; no WebAuthn/passkey affordance was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow password managers immediately and add phishing-resistant passkey/WebAuthn sign-in and recovery.

findings.summary: CSP is permissive and privacy headers are absent
findings.evidence: Headers include unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval in script-src; Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline using nonces or hashes, then add strict Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Core content disappears without JavaScript
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 3% raw/rendered content overlap and classified the page as a JS shell; the crawler view only says JavaScript is required.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core forms/content and use JavaScript as progressive enhancement, with functional HTML submissions where feasible.

findings.summary: Required-field errors are not surfaced humanely
findings.evidence: Empty login submission produced no visible field-level message or error summary despite required fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Use interaction-timed validation, persistent associated messages and accessible error announcement.

findings.summary: Login disables autofill and paste
findings.evidence: DOM/Lighthouse show autocomplete="off" on login fields and active paste prevention on the password field.
findings.suggestedFix: Use username and current-password autocomplete tokens and never intercept paste.

findings.summary: Account access relies on a hostile password flow
findings.evidence: The account entry point provides password-only authentication while blocking paste/autofill, with no observed passkey option.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkeys, preserve password-manager compatibility and keep recovery paths clear and reversible.

findings.summary: Dark preference leaves the portal light-only
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is byte-identical to the default capture and retains white form surfaces; rendered CSS contains no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface, text, border and form-control tokens.

findings.summary: Empty login submission gives no clear field-level recovery
findings.evidence: After activating Login with both required fields empty, the captured form showed no visible error summary or field messages.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, mark fields with aria-invalid, associate concise errors, focus an error summary and announce it through a live region.

findings.summary: Redirects and parser-blocking resources delay content
findings.evidence: HAR recorded two redirects and parser-inserted high-priority scripts; Lighthouse estimates 1.51 s redirect savings, including an HTTP hop.
findings.suggestedFix: Redirect directly to HTTPS login, defer non-critical scripts and shorten the parser-blocking dependency chain.

findings.summary: Footer icons lack accessible alternatives
findings.evidence: Lighthouse and the images probe found four social images without alt text; their links therefore lack robust accessible names.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each social link an accessible name and mark redundant icon images alt="".

findings.summary: Several interactive targets are too small or zero-sized
findings.evidence: The focus probe measured visible login/register controls at only 34 px high and found a zero-size navigation toggle and many zero-size focusable menu links.
findings.suggestedFix: Meet a 44 by 44 CSS pixel target where possible and ensure collapsed controls are neither focusable nor exposed.

findings.summary: Angular throws a console error during load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured Angular $compile:nodomevents from angular-all1.0.js during the login load.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the invalid event directive and add console-error monitoring to prevent regressions.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions
findings.evidence: All five images lack explicit width and height; Lighthouse ties the social icons to observed layout shifts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width and height (or equivalent intrinsic aspect-ratio) on every image.

findings.summary: Some navigation is not crawlable or descriptive
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found JavaScript/# anchors and the link text “here”; DOM extraction also found the Skip to Main Content link implemented as javascript:void(0).
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href targets and descriptive link text for every navigation action.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are missing or inconsistent
findings.evidence: The rendered login document exposes no canonical link; requests for robots.txt/sitemap.xml returned the application shell rather than machine-readable control files.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a canonical URL, valid robots.txt and XML sitemap with consistent indexing policy.

findings.summary: A nationwide public service is exposed as English-only on audited routes
findings.evidence: The rendered documents declare lang="en" but the audited login and public-service templates expose no language selector or alternate-language links; CSS contains many physical left/right offsets.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer supported Indian-language alternatives, publish hreflang, set lang/dir per locale and migrate layout to logical properties.

findings.summary: The login route ships substantial unused code
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 235 KiB unused JavaScript and 22 KiB unused CSS while HAR attributes 454 KiB transferred to scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route, remove unused dependencies and avoid initializing features absent from the current page.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference is not implemented
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no prefers-reduced-motion handling on a page that uses Angular transition/loading effects.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential transitions and loading motion in prefers-reduced-motion safeguards.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences receive no explicit adaptation
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast capture is byte-identical to default and CSS contains no prefers-contrast or forced-colors handling.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast styles that preserve control boundaries and focus visibility.

findings.summary: Route and tab changes use abrupt legacy swaps
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition declarations in this multi-route Angular portal.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route and tab state changes with same-document/cross-document View Transitions, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Large persistent chrome does not respond to scroll state
findings.evidence: Screenshots show a tall fixed header/navigation/footer frame and DOM/CSS contains no scroll-state query or progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state-aware, compact chrome where long forms scroll, while preserving orientation.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS uses global media queries but no container queries across reusable forms and navigation components.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type and component-local @container rules for reused form and navigation modules.
